articles.title: James Bond hopes for Matthew Rhys' scuppered by 'terrible joke'
articles.summary: Matthew Rhys has excelled in many roles recently - but Bond was one that got away after a bad joke.
articles.body:
Hollywood actor Matthew Rhys has told how a "terrible joke" he made during a James Bond audition may have scuppered his chances of being cast in the iconic role.

Rhys went to the offices of the Broccoli family [who produce Bond films] in London to audition for the role in the early 2000s but said he was caught off guard by one particular question.

Appearing on Conan O'Brien's podcast , the actor said he was first asked if he had read Casino Royale before being asked "so what would you do differently with Bond?"

The 51-year-old, from Cardiff, said that "as a terrible joke, I said 'limp'" and the room went quiet "so I thought I would double down and said 'eye patch' and then I just fell apart".

He said the audition for the role of the suave British secret agent lasted about another 30 seconds after that.

Asked by Conan O'Brien how the audition went, Rhys replied "well, I'm not playing Bond, nor have I been".

Daniel Craig was chosen for the role and went on to star in five Bond films, beginning with Casino Royale in 2006.

Rhys said it was terrifying to walk into the building overlooking Green Park in London and seeing so many well-known faces also waiting to audition.

They all sat there "making terrible small talk" before being called in, he said.

Once in front of the panel, he was "trying to remain kind of serious and suave" before his attempt at comedy fell flat.

The audition was "very brief after that" and he reflected "oh, that was my Bond moment and I think of that often".

He said he often wondered what Daniel Craig said to that question.

British actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the new James Bond , taking over from Daniel Craig.

The 40-year-old, who is known for films such as Twilight and The Batman, is the seventh actor to play the famous fictional spy and will star in the 26th Bond movie.

The film is expected to go into production in 2027, before its release in 2028.

Rhys moved to the US to pursue a career in acting and lives in New York with his wife, actress Keri Russell.

He made history at the Emmys in September by becoming the first person to win two lead acting prizes in one night.

He was named best lead actor in a limited series for the psychological thriller The Beast In Me , and best lead actor in a comedy for his role in Widow's Bay .

He has also voiced the role of Han Solo in a new Welsh language adaptation of Star Wars , ahead of the sci-fi classic's 50th anniversary in 2027.

Rhys has previously said he was "too scared" to talk to Harrison Ford about this, describing it as a "surreal" experience to take on such a role.

He said he saw Ford at the Emmys ceremony but did not dare "go over and say, 'guess what I just did? Revoiced you in Welsh'".

articles.title: Exportação de carne bovina bate recorde e encarece produto no Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: As exportações de carne de boi atingiram marcas históricas: US$ 14,2 bilhões de janeiro até outubro, o maior valor já registrado para o período – 8% a mais na comparação com 2025.
articles.summary: Com exportação de carne bovina atingindo US$ 14,2 bilhões, a forte demanda dos EUA e a retenção de fêmeas elevaram os preços nos açougues brasileiros em 12%.
articles.body:
Em 2026, o Brasil bateu recorde de exportações de carne bovina. Só que a alta nas vendas lá fora tem contribuído para o aumento de preços nos açougues daqui.

Do nosso lado da balança comercial, a carne bovina ganha peso. O pecuarista de Barretos, no interior de São Paulo, enxerga um mundo com cada vez menos entraves.

“Conquistando os novos mercados, mostrando que nós temos capacidade de entregar qualidade, com custo interessante para o mercado de maneira tanto nacional quanto internacional”, diz o pecuarista André Perrone.

Em dólares, as exportações de carne de boi atingiram marcas históricas: US$ 14,2 bilhões de janeiro até outubro, o maior valor já registrado para o período – 8% a mais na comparação com 2025. O recorde veio mesmo com o veto da União Europeia à carne brasileira, em setembro, e apesar de termos ultrapassado a cota que vai para a China sem sobretaxa.

Uma das explicações dessa alta é que os Estados Unidos nunca compraram tanta carne bovina do Brasil. Atualmente, o produto está fora do tarifaço americano. É que diante da baixa disponibilidade doméstica de animais para abate e com o aumento da demanda interna, o presidente Trump abriu uma cota extra de importação, sem a cobrança de tarifas adicionais.

“O mercado americano é o maior mercado consumidor do mundo. O Brasil tem ocupado, tem desempenhado esse papel de oferecer para os Estados Unidos um complemento ao consumo americano em um segmento muito específico. O Brasil exporta uma carne magra que é usada pela indústria de alimentos americana para fazer, por exemplo, os hambúrgueres”, afirma Abrão Neto, CEO da Amcham Brasil.

É aí que o Brasil se posiciona como um fornecedor estratégico, segundo Felippe Cauê Serigati, economista da FGV Agro:

“Quem está com carne bovina, com animal disponível, com escala para atender essa demanda? Praticamente, no momento em que a gente conversa, só tem o Brasil”.

Brasil bate recorde de exportações de carne bovina, e vendas para fora fazem com que produto fique mais caro no país — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Não é só no mercado externo que tem demanda. Aqui dentro, o brasileiro também consome muita carne. A questão agora é o preço. Nos últimos 12 meses, a alta é de 12% - bem mais do que o índice geral de inflação. Só em outubro, a alta foi de 2,27%. Reflexo da subida de preços no mercado internacional e do aumento da demanda interna, e também uma influência do próprio ciclo de produção - os pecuaristas reduzem o abate nesta época do ano para focar na reprodução dos animais.

“A gente já está vendo um processo de retenção de fêmeas. O que que isso significa? Olha, uma fração das fêmeas, das vacas, que poderiam ser encaminhadas para o abate, está sendo retida justamente para a produção do bezerro”, explica Felippe Cauê Serigati.

O analista de vendas do agronegócio Gustavo Alves se vira como pode:

“Algumas opções de carne diferente pega, às vezes, uma pecinha um pouco menor de uma, da de outra, e a gente tenta ir fazendo algumas manobras assim para a gente poder comer uma carne bacana e fazer um churrasquinho legal”.

articles.title: Natal Sem Fome 2026: campanha quer arrecadar 2 mil toneladas | G1
articles.standfirst: Com o tema 'Ilumine o Natal de quem precisa', a meta é arrecadar 2 mil toneladas de alimentos e atender 1,5 milhão e meio de brasileiros em situação de vulnerabilidade.
articles.summary: A campanha Natal Sem Fome 2026, da Ação da Cidadania, busca arrecadar alimentos para combater a insegurança alimentar de milhões de pessoas em vulnerabilidade no país.
articles.body:
Começou a campanha Natal Sem Fome para distribuir alimentos a quem precisa em todo o Brasil.

Há uma década, a dona de casa Damiana Alves de Paula foi morar em uma ocupação no Centro do Rio. O que mantém a despensa cheia é a generosidade:

“A gente recebe os legumes e recebe também a alimentação: arroz, feijão, macarrão, farinha, essas coisas todas. Beneficia para caramba”, conta.

As cestas básicas chegam por meio de um projeto chamado Sopão do Bem, que distribui as doações recolhidas pela Ação da Cidadania - a ONG criada pelo sociólogo Betinho há mais de 30 anos para ajudar a matar a fome no Brasil.

Apesar de ter saído do mapa da fome em 2025, 44,8 milhões de brasileiros - cerca de um quinto da população - ainda não têm renda suficiente para manter uma alimentação saudável, segundo o relatório da ONU. A missão da Ação da Cidadania é garantir que mais pessoas tenham comida de qualidade no prato.

Em 2026, mais uma vez, a ONG organiza a campanha Natal sem Fome. Com o tema "Ilumine o Natal de quem precisa", a meta é arrecadar 2 mil toneladas de alimentos e atender 1,5 milhão e meio de brasileiros em situação de vulnerabilidade.

“Você tem a primeira camada da fome, que é calórica, você ter falta de calorias no seu corpo. Essa a gente já está superando. Agora, a gente precisa superar a da qualidade de alimento: nutrientes, vitaminas, sais minerais. Todos os itens que fazem o corpo estar nutrido, e essas outras fomes a gente conseguir exterminar também”, diz Kiko XXX.

Campanha Natal Sem Fome distribui alimentos a quem precisa em todo o Brasil — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O galpão da ONG no Rio ainda está vazio. A cerca de um mês do Natal, é hora de fazer um apelo. Empresas e pessoas físicas podem doar.

Monica Teixeira, repórter: Kiko, a gente quer ver esse galpão lotado. Kiko XXX: Eu também. Meu sonho é ver isso tudo lotado mais uma vez, mais um ano.

A solidariedade é muito bem-vinda na casa da faxineira Maria Pereira da Silva.

“E através dessa doação é que dá certo mesmo, porque se não fosse, dava certo não, minha filha”.

A Maria tem oito filhos. Três moram com ela - além do neto. São as doações de alimentos que garantem cada uma das refeições na casa. No Natal, essa ajuda é como um presente de Papai Noel.

“Você não faz ideia do tanto que eu estou assim ansiosa chegar o dia de receber a cesta básica. Porque, às vezes, é muita coisa boa. Vem até panetone”, conta Maria.

Uma caixa de surpresas que não só mata a fome, também acolhe.

articles.title: Avenida Santa Gleide: trecho no Bugio é interditado para obra | G1
articles.standfirst: Intervenção para reparo em adutora começa às 22h desta segunda-feira (23) e segue até as 18h de terça (24), no bairro Bugio.
articles.summary: A Avenida Santa Gleide, no bairro Bugio, terá bloqueio total na manhã de terça-feira (24) para reparos da Iguá Sergipe, com desvios organizados pela SMTT em Aracaju.
articles.body:
Avenida Santa Gleide em Aracaju — Foto: SMTT/Divulgação

A Avenida Santa Gleide, localizada no bairro Bugio, Zona Norte de Aracaju , passará por alterações no trânsito a partir das 22h desta segunda-feira (23), devido a uma obra emergencial da Iguá Sergipe para o reparo de uma adutora.

Segundo a Superintendência Municipal de Transportes e Trânsito (SMTT), inicialmente o fluxo de veículos funcionará em meia pista, com previsão de conclusão dos trabalhos às 18h desta terça-feira (24).

Nas primeiras horas da manhã de terça-feira (24), a via será totalmente interditada no trecho entre as ruas Carira e Evangelino da Paixão. Durante o bloqueio, os motoristas devem seguir o desvio temporário acessando a Rua Evangelino da Paixão, entrando na Rua Maria da Glória de Andrade, seguindo pela Rua Simone Lima Freire, retornando à Rua Evangelino da Paixão, passando pela Avenida Maria Fonseca de Moraes e, por fim, acessando a Rua Carira para voltar à Avenida Santa Gleide.

De acordo com a SMTT, os desvios serão mantidos durante todo o período da intervenção e equipes estarão no local para organizar o tráfego e garantir a segurança dos trabalhadores. Os condutores devem redobrar a atenção ao passar pela região e respeitar a sinalização.

articles.title: Corais brasileiros: cientistas tentam salvar espécies do El Niño | G1
articles.standfirst: Corais são organismos vivos que servem de refúgio para inúmeras espécies marinhas e são fonte de renda de pescadores do mundo inteiro.
articles.summary: Com o avanço do super El Niño, cientistas coletam corais brasileiros para reprodução assistida no AquaRio, visando repovoar o litoral e evitar a extinção marinha.
articles.body:
Um grupo de cientistas está dedicado a uma missão de emergência no litoral brasileiro: os pesquisadores querem salvar corais ameaçados pelo super El Niño .

Eles estão desaparecendo do planeta. O aquecimento global, que eleva a temperatura das águas, está destruindo os corais - organismos vivos que servem de refúgio para inúmeras espécies marinhas e são fonte de renda de pescadores do mundo inteiro. Mortos, eles ficam brancos.

As imagens são de uma operação de emergência para salvar os corais no Brasil. Desde setembro de 2026, os cientistas estão coletando espécies que só ocorrem no nosso litoral. As 16 mais importantes na formação de recifes são levadas para o laboratório do AquaRio, no Rio de Janeiro.

“Esse é o único lugar do Brasil, autorizado pelo Ministério do Meio Ambiente, a realizar a coleta de várias espécies de corais do nosso litoral em caráter de urgência, antes do auge do fenômeno super El Niño em nosso território. O objetivo é povoar esses berçários de corais, permitindo que eles sejam estudados, a reprodução induzida dessas espécies e, depois, a reintrodução desses corais em lugares do nosso litoral onde a temperatura do mar não seja hostil a essas espécies. Aqui, os corais são recortados em partes menores para formar novas colônias vivas em laboratório”, conta o repórter André Trigueiro.

Cientistas tentam salvar corais ameaçados pelo super El Niño no litoral brasileiro — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

“Nesse momento, a gente está garantindo, espécies de diferentes locais do nosso litoral brasileiro, como se fosse uma Arca de Noé, garantir a sobrevivência dessas espécies ex situ, fora do seu ambiente natural. Para agora, o imediatismo é garantir que essas espécies sejam mantidas vivas aqui no laboratório antes dos efeitos do El Niño”, explica Rafael Franco, diretor técnico do AquaRio.

As imagens feitas há oito anos no litoral da Bahia são raras. Um coral cérebro lançando seus ovos no mar. Hoje, na mesma região, já não é possível encontrar com facilidade essa espécie. Mas, segundo os cientistas, ainda há tempo de salvar esses seres tão importantes para a vida marinha.

“É claro que muita pesquisa científica ainda precisa ser feita em diferentes áreas de conhecimento, mas garantindo uma população saudável e geneticamente saudável, capaz de ser reintroduzida nesses locais previamente mapeados que possam comportar e receber esses animais cultivados aqui no laboratório”, diz Rafael Franco.

articles.title: UVR Filhos do Sol: Belém ganha novo galpão de coleta seletiva | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidade da cooperativa Filhos do Sol fica no bairro da Condor e tem áreas para separação, armazenamento e prensagem de recicláveis. Espaço também ganhou um porto logístico.
articles.summary: A UVR Filhos do Sol conta com mais de mil metros quadrados e estrutura completa para triagem de materiais e apoio aos trabalhadores da reciclagem em Belém.
articles.body:
Galpão de coleta seletiva é entregue em Belém após obras de R$ 2 milhões. — Foto: João Caio

A Prefeitura de Belém entregou, na quarta-feira (18), o galpão da Unidade de Valorização de Recicláveis (UVR) Filhos do Sol , na avenida Bernardo Sayão, no bairro da Condor. O espaço foi recuperado e adaptado para as atividades da cooperativa, com investimento de R$ 2.089.951,88.

Com 1.010,20 metros quadrados, a unidade tem áreas para seleção, estocagem e prensagem de materiais recicláveis, além de instalações administrativas e de apoio aos trabalhadores.

A obra foi executada pela Secretaria Municipal de Obras e Infraestrutura (Seinfra), por meio do Convênio 71, firmado entre a prefeitura e a Itaipu Binacional, com participação da Itaipu Parquetec.

A UVR Filhos do Sol faz parte do projeto Gestão de Resíduos Sólidos, Educação Ambiental e Inovação em Bioeconomia , um dos 37 grandes projetos que tinham data de entrega até a COP 30.

A recuperação da unidade incluiu a adaptação da estrutura existente e a construção de novos espaços. O galpão conta com:

Áreas para seleção, estocagem e prensagem de recicláveis;

Espaços para circulação e manobra de veículos e equipamentos;

O porto foi projetado para facilitar o recebimento, a movimentação e o transporte dos materiais recicláveis.

O espaço também recebeu reforço estrutural, recuperação do piso, melhorias na estrutura metálica, construção de muro de contenção e serviços de acabamento.

UVR integra projeto que prevê quatro entregas

O projeto "Gestão de Resíduos Sólidos, Educação Ambiental e Inovação em Bioeconomia" previa a entrega de 4 unidades de valorização de recicláveis (UVR's).

Veja as organizações contempladas e as datas de entrega informadas:

Cooperativa Filhos do Sol : unidade entregue em novembro de 2026;

Cooperativa dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis (Concaves) : unidade entregue em novembro de 2025 ;

Associação de Catadores da Coleta Seletiva de Belém (ACCSB) : sem data de entrega informada;

Cooperativa de Trabalho dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis das Águas Lindas (Aral) : sem data de entrega informada.

articles.title: Amapá recebe R$ 18 milhões contra seca, queimadas e pragas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo Waldez Góes, contato diário com moradores e prefeituras ajuda a destravar decretos de emergência para crises que atingem o estado. Recurso também paga aluguel de ferry boat para o Bailique.
articles.summary: O ministro Waldez Góes confirmou a ajuda federal no Amapá para 16 municípios afetados pela estiagem, incêndios florestais e a praga vassoura-de-bruxa na mandioca.
articles.body:
Relato de moradores acelerou envio de R$ 18 milhões contra seca, queimadas e praga no Amapá, diz ministro. — Foto: Polícia Civil/Divulgação

O contato direto com moradores das áreas afetadas tem sido decisivo para destravar a ajuda humanitária no Amapá. A afirmação foi feita nesta segunda-feira (23) pelo ministro da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional (MIDR), Waldez Góes, ao destacar o envio de R$ 18 milhões do governo federal para combater emergências ambientais e agrícolas no estado.

Segundo o ministro, o diálogo diário com quem vive na ponta acelera a aprovação dos decretos de emergência nos municípios.

"Eu recebo muita informação de agricultores, de pescadores, de extrativistas, de moradores do campo e da cidade, o que facilita a agilidade na aprovação das situações de emergência e a liberação de recursos para o município e o estado atenderem à sociedade", afirmou Góes nesta segunda-feira (23).

Do total de R$ 18 milhões já disponibilizados pela União, a maior parte foi repassada ao governo estadual, responsável por distribuir a assistência. Pelo menos sete prefeituras também receberam verbas diretamente para enfrentar a estiagem.

Atualmente, o Amapá soma quatro tipos de ocorrências com situação de emergência reconhecida pelo governo federal.

Vassoura-de-bruxa (praga que destrói plantações de mandioca): afeta 15 municípios;

Incêndios florestais : registrados em quatro cidades ( Oiapoque , Laranjal do Jari , Mazagão e Vitória do Jari );

Incêndio urbano : registrado em Oiapoque , após fogo no lixão da cidade.

Ao comentar as queimadas nas matas, o ministro demonstrou preocupação com o avanço do fogo. "Hoje são quatro municípios que vivem esse drama. Esperamos que parem por aí", disse.

Reforço contra queimadas e socorro ao Bailique

Em Laranjal do Jari , município que já recebia verba para combater a seca e a praga na mandioca, o ministério analisa um novo plano de trabalho específico contra os incêndios florestais. O recurso vai custear a contratação de brigadistas, transporte, água e Equipamentos de Proteção Individual (EPIs).

O arquipélago do Bailique, distrito de Macapá afetado pela seca, Góes confirmou que os recursos já estão na conta do governo estadual.

Desta vez, além da compra de água e alimentos, a verba autoriza o aluguel de balsas e embarcações do tipo ferry boat para garantir que as doações cheguem às comunidades isoladas.

articles.title: Vendaval destelha casa em Teresópolis; família é abrigada por vizinhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Moradora mostra destruição causada pela chuva no bairro Pimentel. Família, com duas crianças, tenta conseguir recursos para fazer os reparos e voltar para casa.
articles.summary: Moradora mostra destruição causada pela chuva no bairro Pimentel. Família, com duas crianças, está abrigada na casa de uma vizinha enquanto tenta conseguir recursos para fazer os r
articles.body:
Vendaval arrancou telhado e destruiu móveis, roupas e outros pertences de família de Andréia em Teresópolis — Foto: Alcemar Silvino/Arquivo pessoal

Uma família do bairro Pimentel, em Teresópolis , na Região Serrana do Rio, teve a casa destelhada durante a tempestada que atingiu o município neste domingo (22).

A força do vento também arrancou parte do madeiramento da estrutura. Diversos móveis, roupas e objetos pessoais foram perdidos. A moradora Andréia Gomes Correia da Silva, que está desempregada, não estava com os filhos em casa no momento do vendaval.

Ela e os dois filhos, Miguel Gomes Corrêa da Silva, de 12 anos, e Marcelly Ferreira Gomes de Pinho, de 8 anos, precisaram deixar a residência e está abrigada temporariamente na casa de uma vizinha, enquanto tenta encontrar uma solução para recuperar o imóvel.

“Até agora, a única ajuda concreta que a gente recebeu foram duas cestas básicas. Muitas pessoas entram em contato, dizem que vão ajudar, que vão trazer alguma coisa. A gente está precisando de ajuda de verdade para conseguir recuperar nossa casa e voltar para lá”, conta Andréia.

O vizinho, Alcemar Silvino, jardineiro, gravou um vídeo mostrando os estragos e compartilhou um pedido de ajuda nas redes sociais para mobilizar doações. Ele conta que os moradores da região também estão tentando ajudar a família, dentro das próprias possibilidades.

“Somos todos pessoas simples aqui, mas estamos tentando ajudar a Andréia da maneira que podemos. A gente espera que a Prefeitura também consiga ajudar nos reparos da casa ou consiga um lugar para a família ficar temporariamente. Ela tem um filho transplantado, que precisa de cuidados especiais, e eles estão precisando muito dessa ajuda”, pede Alcemar.

Miguel passou por um transplante de medula há quase um ano. Segundo Andréia, ele não pode permanecer em ambientes com umidade e mofo, o que torna ainda mais urgente a necessidade de recuperar a casa para que a família possa voltar a morar no local com segurança.

Entre os itens danificados estão móveis, roupas, calçados e brinquedos das crianças. A estrutura da residência também precisa de reparos. A moradora pede ajuda com materiais de construção, portas, janelas, móveis e outros itens necessários para reconstruir o que foi perdido.

Outro problema apontado pela moradora é a dificuldade para conseguir o aluguel social. De acordo com Andréia, a Defesa Civil informou que, como a residência não foi interditada, ela não teria direito ao benefício. Com isso, a família continua abrigada na casa da vizinha, sem previsão de quando poderá voltar para o próprio imóvel.

A reportagem entrou em contato com a Prefeitura de Teresópolis para solicitar esclarecimentos sobre a situação do imóvel, a avaliação da Defesa Civil e a possibilidade de assistência à família.

Em nota, o município disse que nos dias 22 e 23 de novembro de 2026, a Secretaria Municipal de Defesa Civil realizou duas vistorias técnicas na residência: a primeira no período noturno, na data da ocorrência, e a segunda na manhã seguinte.

Segundo a Defesa Civil, a força de sucção provocada pela ação dos ventos neste domingo (22) ocasionou o arrancamento das telhas juntamente com o madeiramento de sustentação.

"Durante a inspeção realizada no dia 23, sob condições adequadas de iluminação natural, a equipe técnica constatou sinais aparentes de ausência prolongada de manutenção na estrutura de madeira responsável pelo suporte e pela fixação das telhas. Foi identificada, especificamente, a insuficiência de recobrimento de argamassa para o adequado chumbamento dos caibros na alvenaria, comprometendo a ancoragem do telhado e favorecendo seu deslocamento diante da ação dos ventos".

Ainda segundo a Defesa Civil, "no momento da vistoria, o solicitante já realizava intervenções para a recomposição integral da cobertura. Na ocasião, a Defesa Civil emitiu orientação técnica para a execução de reforços na fixação e na ancoragem do madeiramento à estrutura da edificação, como medida preventiva para evitar a recorrência de situações semelhantes".

Até a última atualização desta reportagem, nenhuma resposta havia sido enviada quanto à possibilidade de assistência à família até que os reparos na casa sejam concluídos.

Chuva provocou seis ocorrências em Teresópolis

De acordo com boletim divulgado pela Defesa Civil às 22h43 deste domingo (22), foram registradas seis ocorrências em diferentes localidades do município.

articles.summary: Presidente dos Estados Unidos afirmou que Gavin Newsom conceceu clemência aos "piores monstros e serial killers" do país em medida do começo de novembro, que converteu 548 penas de
articles.body:
Montagem mostra o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, e o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump — Foto: Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , criticou o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, por sua decisão de comutar as penas de morte de 548 presos no começo desde mês. No discurso, o republicano atacou o democrata, cotado como possível candidato à presidência do país em 2028.

Segundo o americano, a decisão foi uma das maiores injustiças da história do país. A fala aconteceu em um discurso feito no Departamento de Justiça do país, em Washington, nesta segunda-feira (23).

"Há poucos dias, o governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom, concedeu clemência e misericórdia a 548 dos monstros mais perversos que existem", afirmou Trump. "Alguns deles têm níveis de loucura e perversidade que nunca vi antes", afirmou.

Estavam presentes os familiares de vítimas de homicídio. Ao longo do discurso, Trump associou a decisão de Newsom a uma suposta leniência dos democratas com a criminalidade.

O republicano também disse que o governo federal trabalha para tentar reverter a decisão, mas não detalhou quais medidas pretende adotar .

O gabinete de Newsom afirmou, em uma publicação na rede social X, que todos os presos beneficiados pela mudança de pena morrerão na prisão.

Segundo Trump, entre os presos beneficiados estão mais de 110 pessoas condenadas por matar crianças e mais de 100 condenadas por estuprar e assassinar suas vítimas. O presidente também mencionou criminosos responsáveis por assassinatos em série e episódios de tortura.

"Depois que o júri apresentou seu veredicto e o sistema de Justiça determinou uma sentença de morte merecida, Newsom apareceu e tirou dessas famílias o único encerramento que talvez pudessem ter", declarou.

Newsom anunciou no início de novembro planos para converter todas as 548 sentenças de morte na Califórnia para prisão perpétua sem possibilidade de liberdade condicional . Muitas dessas comutações exigem a aprovação da Suprema Corte da Califórnia.

O democrata é um dos cotados para concorrer à Casa Branca em 2028 .

Ele argumentou que a pena de morte é moralmente errada e incompatível com os valores da Califórnia. A Califórnia não realiza uma execução desde 2006, embora os eleitores tenham rejeitado propostas para abolir a pena de morte em 2012 e 2016.

A iniciativa de Newsom gerou críticas de promotores e de algumas famílias das vítimas, enquanto seus defensores argumentam que a pena de morte é onerosa, aplicada de forma desigual e suscetível a condenações injustas.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah visit: India to give $1.62bn economic package
articles.summary: As Nepal rebuilds after deadly floods, its prime minister sets contentious issues aside to secure Indian funding, port access and a new train service.
articles.body:
Nepal's Prime Minister Balen Shah has repeatedly called for his country to be treated as an equal by its powerful neighbours. His first visit to the Indian capital, Delhi, put that approach to the test, as both sides sought to reset a relationship strained by years of friction.

The contrast between the two leaders was striking.

Shah, 36, wearing his trademark black suit and sunglasses, stood beside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, 76, dressed in white. Shah rose to power after a wave of Gen Z-led protests toppled his predecessor.

Modi, meanwhile, is serving a third term and has recently faced student-led protests in India.

Yet, the two leaders seemed determined to project warmer relations. They exchanged gifts, inspected a military guard of honour and jointly flagged off a new cross-border train service.

For Nepal, the stakes were about far more than repairing diplomatic ties.

The two countries announced a series of agreements covering trade, hydropower, transport and education for Nepali youths.

India, more crucially, unveiled a $1.6bn (£1.22bn) support package as Nepal recovers from devastating floods earlier this year.

The floods killed more than 1,400 people, with thousands still missing. Shah's government has faced criticism over support for families which lost homes and loved ones.

The country faces a huge reconstruction challenge. The government estimates rebuilding could cost as much as $4.8bn. Addressing the UN General Assembly in September, Shah warned that when climate disasters devastate poorer countries, "the answer cannot simply be another mega-loan".

Modi pledged nearly $1.6bn in Indian support. Most of it will come as a line of credit for energy projects, alongside about $400m in grants for reconstruction and infrastructure.

While Nepal would have preferred a larger package, former senior Nepali diplomat Vijay Kant Karna says it is still "a significant amount" and could help stabilise a relationship that has often been uneasy.

A Hindu-majority nation wedged between India and China, Nepal has long had to navigate competing interests from its two giant neighbours. Allegations of political interference and an unresolved border dispute have frequently complicated ties with India.

Nepal's former Prime Minister, KP Sharma Oli, who leads a communist party, was widely viewed as being closer to China. Shah, by contrast, emerged as a political outsider when he was elected earlier this year. The former rapper, then 35, led a party that was only four years old.

His new approach of dealing with India may explain why the border dispute was largely absent from the leaders' public remarks, although the joint statement acknowledged that outstanding issues remained.

According to Govind Pokharel, a former vice-chairman of Nepal's National Planning Commission, Shah's government may have chosen to set contentious issues aside in order to secure progress on more immediate development needs.

"Right now you can go home and convince the young Nepalis that it will be handled later," Pokhrel says, "but if they don't deal with these issues in the future, there will be criticism."

Veteran Indian diplomat Anil Trigunayat says both sides appear to have opted to leave the dispute to established mechanisms rather than engage in what he calls "cartographic aggressions".

There were other gains for Nepal as a result of the Delhi visit.

As a landlocked country heavily dependent on India for trade, Nepal secured access to two additional Indian ports, Kandla and Paradip. The two sides also agreed to improve road and rail connectivity.

The leaders jointly inaugurated a train service linking Ayodhya in India, revered by Hindus as the birthplace of Lord Ram, with Janakpur in Nepal, traditionally regarded as the birthplace of his wife Sita.

There was, however, disappointment on aviation.

Nepal has long sought greater access to Indian airspace in order to attract international traffic to its airports at Bhairahawa and Pokhara.

Some analysts believe the lack of an agreement reflects Indian concerns over Chinese involvement in the two airport projects.

"The airport in Pokhara can pose certain security challenges for India, so it is a more complicated issue to resolve," says Trigunayat.

India did, however, agree to make an existing air route linking Kathmandu, Bhairahawa and Lucknow bidirectional.

"Nepal invested a huge amount of money in those airports," says Pokharel. "It fell short of expectations, but the bidirectional route is a breakthrough."

Shah must now manage relations with China as he seeks to balance the interests of Nepal's two much larger neighbours.

For now he returns home with substantial financial commitments from India as Nepal continues the long task of rebuilding.

articles.title: Blaina girl Lilly Jones stabbed by 14-year-old boy, murder trial told
articles.summary: Lilly Jones's body was found near Duffryn Park in Blaina two days after she was reported missing.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains details readers may find distressing

A teenage girl was stabbed "around 55 times" by a 14-year-old boy, a murder trial has been told.

Lilly Jones, from Blaina, in Blaenau Gwent, left home at about 18:30 on 20 June, telling her father she was "popping out for a bit".

Her body was discovered face down in woodland close to Duffryn Park two days later.

A 14-year-old boy, who cannot be named because he is under 18, denies her murder.

He and Lilly shared an interest in Pokémon and were "in some kind of relationship", the court heard.

The boy was dressed in a white short-sleeved shirt and tie as he sat in the dock at Newport Crown Court on Monday.

Anna Pope KC, prosecuting, told the jury a camping knife containing a complete DNA profile had been found in the boy's bedroom drawer.

"It was calculated to be a billion times more likely if this DNA had come from Lilly Jones than if it had come from someone else," she said.

Pope said the boy had not given an explanation as to why Lilly's DNA was on the knife.

She added scratch marks were discovered on the inside of his arm and forensic swabs taken from Lilly's fingernails identified his DNA.

She had been stabbed in the heart, both lungs and an artery in her neck. There were 17 stab wounds to her neck, and knife wounds were found on her face, jaw, chest and bottom.

Newport Crown Court was told Lilly and the boy became friends in March this year after a chance meeting in the street.

They were captured on CCTV cameras in Blaina and were last seen together at 18:50 as they walked towards a footbridge leading to the park, near to where her body was later found.

At 22:19 that evening, Lilly's family contacted the police to report her missing. It was the day after her 14th birthday.

Police searching for Lilly spoke to the teenager the following day. He told officers he was supposed to meet up with Lilly at the Red Lion pub in Blaina, but she never arrived.

He later told police they had been together for part of the previous night, before they separated. He said he came home after she told him she was going to meet up with someone else.

In a further conversation with police on the day Lilly's body was found, he said she had told him she wanted to show him a disused park, before leaving.

When he was arrested he told police he did not murder Lilly and did not know where her phone was.

The trial heard that, when a phone belonging to the defendant was examined, he was found to have searched for Gwent Police, and similar terms, about 30 times the morning after Lilly disappeared, between 05:49 and 10:02.

Pope added: "The phone also showed that photographs had been taken by someone using [the defendant's] phone, we say that's [the defendant]."

She added it was "of note" that one of the photographs "is looking back towards the scene where we say Lilly's body was later found".

Addressing the jury, Pope said: "We will ask you to consider why it is that [the defendant] would take a photograph of some distance, of the area where we know Lilly to have died that night? Particularly if, as he suggests, he left her alive, when she was going to meet a friend."

articles.title: Kansas family tears down a ‘Magic Treehouse’ built for neighbourhood children after the city orders its removal from public land; a petition to save it gathered 592 signatures
articles.summary: The Larsen family in Kansas tore down the treehouse they built beside the Redbud Trail after the city of Andover told them it stood on public land and had
articles.body: The Larsen family in Kansas tore down the treehouse they built beside the Redbud Trail after the city of Andover told them it stood on public land and had been installed without prior approval. Built in spring 2026, the structure grew from a play space for the family's sons into a gathering spot for children from the neighbourhood and beyond. A petition to save it gathered 592 signatures and won the backing of Magic Tree House author Mary Pope Osborne, yet the family took the treehouse down themselves on Sunday, 15 November 2026, the city's deadline.Who built the Magic Treehouse and how it became a favourite meeting place for childrenAccording to FOX Kansas News, Ezra Larsen, who was nine when the report was published, helped design and build the treehouse with his grandfather. His brother, Elam, said that people who use the trail, including some from outside Andover, also came to play there.The Wichita Eagle described the treehouse as standing outside the family's fence but behind their house. In August, the city administrator signed a letter to the family asking them not to construct or install any improvements on Redbud Trail property, or on any city-owned or maintained land, without first contacting the city and receiving written authorisation.A petition, a speech from the Larsen sons and an attempt at compromise before the city deadlineAfter the letter arrived, the family started a petition and took their case to the city council. Tatiana Larsen spoke at a council meeting and tried to reach a compromise, but the deadline arrived without one. Her sons, Elam and Ezra, also addressed the council in October, where Elam told councillors that removing the treehouse would affect many other people who would not like the decision.Larsen told The Eagle that none of it was for the family's own benefit, and that her children's play barely scratched the surface of how much the community used it. She said she has video of about 15 teenagers and children gathered around the swing and the treehouse, a scene so emotional to watch that it brought tears to her eyes.Removal day, a farewell message and the Larsens' willingness to discuss a replacement with the cityIn a Facebook post on removal day, Larsen wrote that the family had tried and wished the treehouse could have stayed. She added that she hopes treehouses like theirs will find homes in other places and bring joy and wonder to more children. She said her children woke up, went outside and were in tears.Larsen said she hopes the city sees the value in spaces like this one, and that the treehouse might prove a stepping stone to a larger idea. She told the newspaper she would welcome the chance to talk to the city about creating a space to replace it. articles.title: Israeli strikes kill at least three, including UNRWA worker, in Gaza
articles.summary: Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 ‘ceasefire’ deal.
articles.body:
Israeli air strikes have killed at least three people in Gaza, including a worker for the UN Palestinian refugee agency, according to the relief agency and local health officials.

The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) on Monday named the worker killed as Adel al-Helo.

He was working near a well in the Jabalia refugee camp in the enclave’s north when hit, the agency and medics said. Three others were wounded in the strike.

Later on Monday, another Israeli air strike ⁠targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two people and wounding others, medics said, according to the Reuters news agency. The Israeli military did not immediately comment.

Israel continues to launch attacks across the enclave, despite an October 2025 “ceasefire” deal with Hamas, which formally halted around two years of fighting but has failed to bring Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza to an end.

“The initial reports indicate that the strike hit a target on the street near the water well, which was manned by UNRWA staff and a guard. The staff were engaged in their regular duties associated with water well operations,” an UNRWA spokesperson told Reuters.

Israel has yet to respond to the incident. But since the October ceasefire, at least 1,679 Palestinian people and five Israeli soldiers have been killed.

Israeli forces have also continued to destroy residential buildings in Gaza, beyond the “Yellow Line” to which they were required to withdraw under the ceasefire.

Al Jazeera journalist Moath al-Kahlout, reporting from Deir el-Balah, said displaced Palestinians who live in the area near the line gathered on Saturday to demonstrate against Israel’s intensifying air strikes.

“More than 500 housing units have been destroyed in less than a month,” Mohammed Musleh, mayor of Deir el-Balah’s Maghazi municipality, told Al Jazeera.

“This is part of what appears to be a systematic policy of gradual creeping displacement aimed at forcing residents out of their camp and destroying as many homes as possible,” he added.

articles.title: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
articles.summary: Interests of oil-producing countries, a US boycott and a dispute over finance may have torpedoed climate talks.
articles.body:
Some may have found it ironic that the world's biggest conference on climate change should collapse over the very mention of fossil fuels - the main cause of global warming.

Yet that is what happened in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.

The failure tells us something about the state of climate diplomacy. But it may tell us even more about the increasingly divided world in which the negotiations take place.

Chris Bowen, the Australian minister who led the negotiations, spoke of a backdrop constituting "the most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory". The competing demands, he said, had become "unbridgeable red lines".

Murat Kurum, Turkey's environment minister and the summit's president, was blunter. Governments should not disappoint people desperate for climate action, he suggested, by getting "hung up on one word or phrase".

And Kurum had a point. Three years ago, at COP28 in Dubai, there was agreement to transition away from fossil fuels. The proposed Antalya Pact failed to mention them at all.

Was it really worth sacrificing the agreement over two words, then?

The countries that rejected it said the distinction was fundamental. They argued that there was a world of difference between promising to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and committing to move away from the fuels responsible for most of them. Without that explicit commitment, they feared the new agreement would weaken the one made in Dubai.

Normally, it is difficult to establish exactly who has said what at these conferences. Much of the bargaining takes place behind closed doors, and governments are often reluctant to admit which proposals they have opposed.

This time, some of the opposition was public - mostly from oil-producing nations.

Mohammad Ayoub, a Saudi negotiator speaking on behalf of the 22 Arab League countries, argued that Arab nations had contributed less than 2% of historical greenhouse gas emissions. It was wealthy industrialised nations, he said, that bore the overwhelming responsibility for the problem.

He defended the Arab countries' right to choose how to tackle climate change according to their national circumstances.

Russia's delegate Sergei Kononuchenko went further. Cutting oil and gas supplies before demand fell, he warned, would cause shortages, higher prices and energy poverty.

"For that reason, we cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel," he said.

The wider political backdrop was still more revealing.

The US, which in previous rounds of talks had helped broker compromises - sometimes working alongside China - had no official delegation in Antalya. President Donald Trump has rejected the entire international climate process.

And while delegates argued over fossil fuels in Turkey, Trump, China's President Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin issued a joint declaration in Shenzhen that included a pledge to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products.

The priorities of some of the world's most powerful governments appeared very different from those being discussed in the negotiating rooms.

Yet, perhaps, the picture is more optimistic than it first appears. About 130 governments backed a demand for explicit language on moving away from fossil fuels - roughly two-thirds of the countries represented in Antalya.

Christiana Figueres, who led the UN negotiations that delivered the Paris Agreement, argued that countries were right to walk away rather than endorse a weaker political commitment that might undermine the progress already made.

Looked at this way, the collapse is not evidence that the world has lost its appetite for climate action. Quite the opposite - a substantial majority of governments were demanding more ambitious action.

So why not simply find a way for them to move ahead without waiting for the countries determined to block them?

The difficulty becomes clearer when you look beyond the dispute over fossil fuels.

Kononuchenko had another target in his sights: climate finance. Much of the money wealthy countries provide to poorer nations, he complained, comes as loans rather than grants. He said that developing countries ended up repaying more than they received.

"This is an old colonial distribution of labour under a new banner," he declared.

Then, in a striking moment, he leaned towards the microphone and switched from Russian into English to address his criticism directly to the Europeans: "First of all distinguished representatives of the EU."

Russia has its own reasons for attacking Europe, but the complaint about finance is one that many developing countries share. They argue that they are being asked to pay for damage they did little to cause while receiving too little help to adapt to climate change or build cleaner economies.

The EU had ruled out significant new funding before the negotiations began. Mohamed Adow, the Kenyan campaigner who heads Power Shift Africa, accused Europe of rejecting a flawed deal while refusing to acknowledge its own responsibility for the failure on finance.

So is it possible for a majority of countries to outvote those blocking progress?

The UN climate chief, Simon Stiell, has acknowledged the need to "improve, modernise and reform" the process. Some governments have proposed introducing voting when consensus proves impossible. Others want countries prepared to move faster to make their own agreements outside the formal talks.

But there is a reason the UN climate process depends on consensus. International climate co-operation is largely voluntary.

Voting might produce more ambitious agreements on paper, but would it persuade the governments that had been outvoted to act? Consensus also offers some protection to smaller and poorer nations that might otherwise find themselves overruled by the most powerful countries.

Meanwhile, the failure to agree a summit declaration does not mean climate action stops. Solar panels, batteries and electric vehicles are becoming increasingly competitive, while the upheaval in global oil and gas supplies is giving countries another reason to generate their own electricity rather than depend on imported fossil fuels.

The energy transition is moving forward, whatever happens in the UN negotiating rooms. The problem is that it is not moving nearly fast enough for the climate.

Longest-ever UN climate talks end with no deal as deep divisions exposed

Five takeaways from the failed climate talks COP31

Perhaps the most poignant aspect of the failed Antalya Pact is what the countries had apparently been prepared to accept.

The final draft expressed "deep concern" that global warming was expected to exceed 1.5°C in the next few years. It warned that further warming would cause increasingly serious damage, some of it irreversible, and called for urgent action to limit how far temperatures rose above that threshold.

This remarkably strong language had survived into the final version, apparently without provoking the opposition that sank the agreement. Even countries bitterly divided over fossil fuels and finance seemed prepared to acknowledge the scale of the danger.

Yet they couldn't agree on how to respond.

And that, perhaps, is what Antalya tells us about the state of international climate co-operation. The problem isn't simply finding the right words or changing the voting rules. It is persuading countries with very different interests to take action that no international authority can compel them to take.

That was always going to be difficult. In today's divided world, it looks harder than ever.

articles.title: Proposed ban on live lobster boiling gets chefs, restaurateurs worked up
articles.summary: A proposed ban would outlaw boiling live crustaceans in one major city, but chefs and restaurant owners call the animal cruelty bill out of touch.
articles.body: A newly introduced New York City Council proposal aims to change how restaurants prep seafood, but the measure is already facing strong pushback from culinary professionals who call it unnecessary and out of touch with real-world kitchen practices. The proposed legislation was introduced by Council members Oswald Feliz and Harvey Epstein. If enacted, it would amend Chapter 15 of Title 17 of the NYC Administrative Code to make it illegal for food service establishments to place live crustaceans — including lobsters and crabs — directly "into boiling liquid for cooking." Citing animal welfare concerns and research regarding crustacean pain sensitivity, the bill mandates alternative prep or humane slaughter methods. LOBSTER ROLL WAR ERUPTS IN NEW ENGLAND OVER CONTROVERSIAL INGREDIENT IN 'DIE-HARD' DIVIDE Under the bill's terms, the mandate would take effect 180 days after becoming law. First-time violations would result in an official warning, while subsequent offenses would carry civil fines of up to $100 per violation. "Boiling any animal alive is animal cruelty," Feliz told the New York Post. "I also want to be clear: this bill does not remove lobster from the menu or prevent anyone from eating it. Everyone is completely free to enjoy as much lobster as they want." CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER While animal welfare advocates support the bill, many in the culinary world argue that the legislation targets a non-issue. Florida-based celebrity chef Jason Smith, who won the Food Network's "Holiday Baking Championship" in 2019 and is a contestant on Fox's "The Floor," questioned why city leaders are focusing on restaurant pots rather than municipal priorities, calling the proposed ban unnecessary. "My argument is that if the city wants restaurants to change how they prepare lobster, it should bring chefs and restaurant owners into the conversation." "The real question is why are these people not doing their real jobs and trying to work harder for the people that voted and put them there," Smith told Fox News Digital. "I'm sure there are more pressing matters than a seafood boiling ban." CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Restaurateur Zach Erdem, owner of 75 Main in Southampton, told Fox News Digital that if city officials want to change kitchen practices, they need to include industry leaders in the conversation to address practical realities. "I understand why people object to boiling lobsters alive," Erdem said. "My argument is that if the city wants restaurants to change how they prepare lobster, it should bring chefs and restaurant owners into the conversation. Show us which methods meet the city's animal welfare goals, what they cost and how a small kitchen can put them into practice during a busy dinner service." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Erdem also noted that legislative bandwidth would be better spent addressing the heavy financial and administrative hurdles small business owners face when trying to operate in New York. "When I look at opening in Manhattan, I look at rent, payroll, food costs and how long it takes to get permits," Erdem pointed out. Every month you're waiting to open is another month you're paying rent without serving a single customer."

articles.title: Hugh Jackman’s $28.75 million New York apartment with ex-wife Deborra-Lee Furness finds a buyer; former couple bought the five-bedroom home for $21 million in 2008
articles.summary: Hugh Jackman and his former wife, Deborra-Lee Furness, appear to be nearing the end of another chapter of their shared life, with their sprawling New York
articles.body: Hugh Jackman and his former wife, Deborra-Lee Furness, appear to be nearing the end of another chapter of their shared life, with their sprawling New York City apartment reportedly entering into a contract. The luxurious West Village property, which the former couple once shared during their marriage, was recently relisted for $28.75 million after previously being offered for rent.The development comes amid Jackman’s relationship with his former Broadway co-star Sutton Foster, with whom he made his Met Gala debut as a couple earlier this year.Jackman, 58, and Furness, 70, purchased the palatial five-bedroom apartment in 2008 for $21 million. The property was first put on the market in June 2022, with an asking price of $38.9 million. However, the listing was withdrawn just two months later.The former couple then explored the rental market, offering the apartment for $125,000 a month in September 2023, around the time they announced their separation. According to sources cited by Realtor.com, the property was leased to a tenant who was expected to stay until December 2026.Those plans appeared to change when the apartment returned to the market on March 31, this time with a reduced asking price of $28.75 million. It has now reportedly found a prospective buyer and entered into a contract. The final sale price has not been disclosed.Although the listing does not identify Jackman and Furness as the owners, property records show that the apartment remains registered under the limited liability company they used to purchase it. The listing also mentions that only limited showings are available to prospective buyers.A sprawling Manhattan home with stunning Hudson River viewsDesigned by acclaimed architect Richard Meier, the three-storey residence on Perry Street spans 11,000 square feet. Described in its listing as a “modernist masterpiece”, the apartment features a dramatic double-height living room, expansive windows overlooking the Hudson River and a striking spiral staircase connecting its three levels.The eighth floor features a large recreation room, a terrace and a library that can also serve as an additional guest room. Four of the five main bedrooms are located on this level, each with an en-suite bathroom.The next floor houses the apartment’s impressive great room, along with a den, lounge, professional-grade kitchen and separate dining room. The entire 10th floor is dedicated to the primary suite, which includes a spa-style bathroom, sauna, workout room, two dressing rooms and a private terrace.Residents also have access to the building’s fitness centre and dining services from celebrity chef Jean-Georges Vongerichten’s Perry St. restaurant, located within the property.What happens to the former couple’s other properties?The apartment is among the properties Jackman and Furness acquired during their marriage. As part of their divorce agreement, the former spouses also dealt with a sprawling penthouse on Eleventh Avenue, which they purchased for $21.12 million in 2022.That property was transferred to a limited liability company linked solely to Furness around the time their divorce was finalised. The reported transaction was valued at roughly half of the apartment’s estimated $23 million worth, suggesting that Furness may have paid Jackman for his share.It remains unclear how the proceeds from the potential sale of the Perry Street apartment will be divided between the former couple.Hugh Jackman and Sutton Foster’s relationshipThe property development comes as Jackman’s relationship with Sutton Foster attracts attention. The two actors first sparked romance rumours after working together in the Broadway revival of The Music Man, which began previews in December 2021.Jackman and Furness announced their separation in September 2023 after 27 years of marriage. In a joint statement at the time, they said they had decided to part ways to pursue individual growth, adding that they would approach the next chapter with gratitude, love and kindness.Foster, meanwhile, filed for divorce from her husband, screenwriter Ted Griffin, in October 2024, after 10 years of marriage. Jackman and Foster later confirmed their relationship in 2025.In May 2025, Furness spoke about the painful end of her marriage in an emotional statement to the Daily Mail, referring to the experience as a journey of betrayal. She said her belief in a higher power had helped her navigate the breakdown of a marriage that had lasted nearly three decades.Jackman and Foster made their Met Gala debut as a couple in May 2026, arriving hand in hand at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Jackman wore a classic tuxedo, while Foster opted for a shimmering gold gown.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: A California student’s essay was flagged 76% AI-generated by Turnitin; his father sued the school after a supervised rewrite earned a D and lowered his final grade to a C, but later dropped the case
articles.summary: A high school student's English essay became the centre of a dispute between his family and a California school district after software flagged much of
articles.body: A high school student's English essay became the centre of a dispute between his family and a California school district after software flagged much of his work as potentially written with artificial intelligence. The student had submitted an assignment on Arthur Miller's The Crucible, but his teacher questioned its originality after an AI detection report indicated that 76% of the text had been generated or influenced by AI. He was asked to complete the work again under classroom conditions. The rewritten assignment received a D, lowering his final grade in the class to a C. His father, Takashi Kato, has now taken the school district to federal court, arguing that the accusation and the grading process were unfair.California student accused of using AI in English essayThe dispute centres on a sophomore at Palo Alto High School in California. He submitted an essay on The Crucible, the play by American dramatist Arthur Miller that examines the Salem witch trials, on October 30, 2025. Around two weeks later, the student uploaded the work to Turnitin, a platform used by the school district to examine student submissions for possible AI involvement.According to the complaint, English teacher Sarah Bartlett informed the student that Turnitin had flagged 76% of his essay as AI-generated or AI-influenced. She also raised questions about his use of Grammarly, alleging that he had acknowledged using the tool to look up synonyms. His father disputed this account.Bartlett's approach allowed students whose assignments were flagged to complete the work again in person. The practice was described as non-punitive, but Kato argues that it effectively placed the burden on his son to prove that he had written the original essay himself.School's AI detection process challenged over student's lower gradeThe student completed the assignment again under classroom conditions. The new submission received a D, according to the lawsuit, bringing his final grade in the subject down to a C.Kato argues that the school did not have a formal academic procedure governing such cases and that the decision to make his son repeat the work was not supported by a proper evaluation of the original submission. He has questioned why a software-generated percentage was allowed to carry so much weight in determining whether the student had used AI.The father also maintains that the school did not give his son a meaningful opportunity to challenge the accusation before requiring him to redo the assignment. The lawsuit describes the grading decision as arbitrary and says the procedure had consequences beyond the individual essay.Father submits nearly 1,200 pages to challenge the allegationKato attempted to contest the teacher's assessment by providing school officials with a substantial collection of material. The submission reportedly included nearly 1,200 pages of supporting evidence, among them working drafts, handwritten notes and access to the document's revision history.The material was intended to show how the essay developed and provide a record of the student's writing process. The family continued discussions with school officials but remained dissatisfied with the district's handling of the matter.At one stage, Kato's family gave the school a deadline of March 6 to award the student a neutral B grade. The district did not accept the demand, according to the report by Palo Alto Online.The disagreement eventually moved beyond the question of one English assignment. Kato is seeking to have the student's grade restored to a B and the AI-related allegation removed from his academic record. He has also requested an independent assessment of the rewritten essay and wants the district to stop using the in-person retake practice.Lawsuit questions AI detector accuracy and alleged school biasThe complaint raises several legal issues, including alleged discrimination, retaliation, lack of due process and improper grading procedures. Kato believes his son was treated unfairly because he is a multilingual Asian male. He also alleges that other students experienced similar accusations, including another Asian student.The father has further claimed that his son faced retaliatory treatment after the family challenged the school's decision. These remain allegations in the lawsuit and have not been established by a court.The complaint also questions the reliability of AI-writing detection software, particularly when it is used to make decisions that could affect a student's academic record. Kato argues that the Turnitin result was treated as decisive evidence rather than one indicator that required further examination.In the filing, the family refers to academic research and university policies that have raised concerns about the accuracy of AI detectors, including the possibility of unfair results for people who do not write English as their first language. It also points to universities that have moved away from using the technology because of concerns about its reliability and fairness.AI-writing dispute raises concerns over student's college prospectsFor Kato, the consequences may extend beyond the student's current classroom performance. He believes the lower grade and the allegation of AI use could affect his son's academic record and potentially create difficulties during the college admissions process.The lawsuit also describes the family's frustration with the way the complaint was handled, citing delays, disagreements over the sequence of events and the school's reliance on the disputed claim about Grammarly. Kato says the experience caused emotional and procedural harm to his family.The father wants the district to reassess the grading decision and address the procedures teachers follow when an AI detector flags student work. His legal challenge also seeks to prevent the school from continuing the in-person retake practice in its current form.Palo Alto Unified School District had not filed a response to the complaint at the time of the May 11, 2026 report. The district also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A case management conference was scheduled for August 6, 2026, according to the report.Father drops lawsuit after school district denies allegationsThe legal dispute continued for several months after Kato filed the complaint in May 2026. In June, Palo Alto Unified School District denied the allegations, with its lawyers arguing that the teacher's grading decisions were within her authority and that the claims of discrimination were unsupported by evidence.Kato eventually dropped the lawsuit on September 2, according to court documents. The district said there was no settlement, financial payment or agreement to change the student's grade, academic record or school policies.The family's attorney, Evan Nelson, told the Palo Alto Daily Post that the student had transferred to another school. He also said the student eventually received a B in the class. The case was dismissed without a court ruling on the allegations of discrimination or the accuracy of Turnitin's AI detection result.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports, court documents and statements from the parties involved. The Times of India has not independently verified the allegations made in the lawsuit, which was voluntarily dismissed without a court ruling on its merits.You use AI every day. articles.title: Poland to get NATO early-warning aircraft after Russian missiles hit country
articles.summary: NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning system aircraft to Poland as part of its response to ⁠three missiles landing in the country.
articles.body: NATO will deploy an AWACS early-warning system aircraft to Poland as part of its response to ⁠three missiles landing in the country on the military alliance’s eastern flank, a Polish deputy defense minister said on Monday. Three Russian Kh-101 missiles ⁠landed in Poland ​on ⁠Friday, prosecutors said, adding to fears that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spill ⁠into NATO territory. “An AWACS early-warning aircraft ​will ⁠be made available to Poland,” ‌Pawel Zalewski told reporters after a NATO meeting in Brussels. “This is a very ‌good system that gives us ‌even deeper... operational awareness which allows us to respond better to this kind of threat.” With their distinctive ⁠nine-meter-wide radar domes, NATO’s 14 Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft have served as the alliance’s eyes in the sky since 1982. Based at Geilenkirchen air base in Germany, the fleet has played an important role ‌in surveillance missions along NATO’s eastern ​flank since Russia launched its ‌full-scale invasion of Ukraine in ⁠2022. In a conflict, they can ⁠provide a common radar picture for allied fighters, ships ‌and control ​centers, while directing NATO combat ‌jets to their ​targets.

articles.title: Canadian couple went to New Zealand for 14-day vacation, had to spend 14 months as they were jailed when their luggage tag was switched onto a bag carrying meth
articles.summary: A Canadian couple spent more than 14 months stranded in New Zealand after being accused of drug smuggling when a luggage tag bearing their details was
articles.body: A Canadian couple spent more than 14 months stranded in New Zealand after being accused of drug smuggling when a luggage tag bearing their details was allegedly found on a suitcase containing methamphetamine. The married couple had travelled from Toronto Pearson International Airport to Auckland in January 2025 for what was supposed to be a 14-day holiday. Instead, they spent five weeks in a New Zealand prison and another 13 months on bail in a monitored facility, which they had to pay for themselves.Their Toronto-based lawyer, Paul Miller, said the couple were eventually acquitted after a trial lasting about two weeks. According to what they told him, the jury deliberated for less than five minutes before the charges were dismissed.Even after the verdict, the couple could not immediately return to Canada because last-minute airfares were prohibitively expensive. They remained in New Zealand for another three weeks until they could afford to fly home, Miller said.The ordeal has drawn attention to an alleged luggage-tag switching operation at Toronto Pearson, in which criminals are suspected of transferring genuine passengers' baggage tags onto suitcases containing drugs.Wife allegedly denied pain medication, husband lost his jobThe couple's lawyer said the experience had taken a severe emotional and financial toll on them. Miller said the wife was denied access to her pain medication during the ordeal, while both spouses had to wear ankle-monitoring devices while out on bail. The husband also lost his job in the skilled trades, according to Cassandra De Marco, a junior lawyer working with Miller.Miller described the emotional distress suffered by the couple as severe, saying it was difficult to imagine what they went through while facing drug-smuggling allegations in a foreign country.How the alleged luggage-tag switching racket worksThe alleged method involves a person with access to airport baggage areas bringing a suitcase containing narcotics into the airport and attaching an unsuspecting passenger's luggage tag to it. The tag carries the passenger's travel and destination details, making the drug-filled suitcase appear to belong to that traveller. If the suitcase passes through customs, an alleged accomplice at the destination airport can collect it. But if authorities intercept the drugs, the passenger whose name is on the tag can become the focus of the investigation. The couple's case is among a growing number of incidents involving passengers who say their luggage tags were transferred to bags containing narcotics.Miller said he was representing 11 alleged victims when a recent documentary investigation by CTV's W5 aired. The number of confirmed and potential clients had since risen to 21, he said. The cases involve travellers accused of transporting narcotics from Toronto to destinations including Brazil, Aruba, Germany, Sri Lanka, Australia, the Dominican Republic and New Zealand.The Toronto couple's case has also drawn attention to that of another Canadian, Tommy Moyeen, who was arrested at the same Auckland airport nine days after the couple's detention. Moyeen was convicted and sentenced to nearly 10 years in prison. He has been in custody in New Zealand for almost two years and has said he intends to challenge his conviction.You use AI every day. articles.title: Andrew received £750,000 from Turkish millionaire, court told
articles.summary: The former Duke of York is expected to give evidence in the complex court case next month.
articles.body:
A Turkish millionaire has told the High Court she was misled over a £750,000 payment she made to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor in 2019.

Nebahat Isbilen is alleging her former business adviser, Selman Turk, misappropriated £38m of her assets, including a payment to the then-Duke of York which she believed was for help with her passport.

Turk has rejected the allegations, saying the 81-year-old Isbilen knew the money was actually being paid in the hope that Mountbatten-Windsor could help her husband, a politician who is in prison in Turkey.

Mountbatten-Windsor repaid the £750,000 and is expected to give evidence to the High Court in December. He is not accused of any wrongdoing.

Isbilen's lawyers also told the court on Monday that Turk had instructed a separate £15,000 payment to Mountbatten-Windsor's ex-wife, Sarah Ferguson, purportedly for the former Duchess of York's 60th birthday party in 2019, and an unquantified "wedding gift" payment for their daughter Princess Beatrice.

Isbilen's family founded a major soap and cosmetics firm in Turkey.

But when her husband, Ilhan, a former member of the Turkish parliament, was arrested in 2015, she wanted help moving her assets out of Turkey. Her lawyers said the charges were "politically motivated" and that in 2017 she was facing "political persecution".

She left Turkey for Greece in 2017 and moved to London in 2018.

Simon Colton KC, representing Isbilen, said she met Turk in January 2017 and gave him control of most of her financial assets.

But Turk "deliberately and systematically abused" her trust and transferred the money to companies he owned or controlled, Colton added.

Colton added that Isbilen approved the £750,000 payment to Andrew, but that Turk "lied to her" about its purpose, which was "a further example of his dishonesty".

The court heard that Isbilen had a private dinner with the then Duke and Duchess of York at Turk's flat in December 2019 where she discussed her husband's case.

Turk's lawyers told the court that Isbilen understood and directed the management of her own affairs.

Joshua Hitchens, representing Turk, said in written submissions: "In circumstances where the claimant dined with the duke and duchess and discussed her husband with them, she cannot have believed that the £750,000 was a disguised fee for help with a passport, or with a visa."

The trial before Mr Justice Adam Johnson is due to conclude in March, with a written judgment at a later date.
